subdomain: 4.1 Define evaluation metrics (accuracy, latency, cost, safety, security)

en.question: A change-request assistant must produce usable drafts within a completion-time target and budget. The security owner also requires zero successful cross-account reads in the defined attack suite. Which release scorecard preserves all of these requirements?

options.text: Rank variants by a weighted average of draft quality, speed, cost, and security.
options.note: A weighted average can let inexpensive, high-quality drafts compensate for a successful cross-account read. That violates the stated security acceptance gate.

options.text: Gate on security and rank the remaining variants by API response success rate.
options.note: Passing security is necessary, but API response success does not establish draft usability, application completion time, or budget compliance.

options.text: Gate on security, then check draft quality, completion latency, and outcome cost separately.
options.note: Separate measurements preserve the quality, latency, and cost requirements while preventing a security failure from being averaged away. The thresholds come from this application's requirements, not a universal benchmark.

options.text: Gate on draft quality and require the combined latency-and-cost score to improve.
options.note: This omits the independent security gate and can hide a latency-target violation behind cost savings. Improvement in a combined score is not compliance with each stated requirement.

references.title: Anthropic: Define success criteria and build evaluations
